title: Fairshare crediting and eviction-avoidance plan for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After last week's capacity event we observed sustained eviction spikes driven by one large workload that silently consumed KV cache and prevented prefix reuse for colocated customers. This ticket designs and implements a fairshare crediting mechanism and a conservative eviction-avoidance policy to reduce noisy-neighbor-induced evictions without sacrificing throughput for steady tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction rate for affected pools reduced by >= 70% during synthetic noisy load tests compared to baseline
No more than 5% regression in average tail latency (P95/P99) for steady tenants under mixed load tests
Telemetry: new fairshare metrics (credits granted, credits consumed, credit deficit) appear in Console dashboards and alerts fire on credit starvation
Rollback plan documented and tested with canary rollout on 1 pool before fleet-wide rollout
tasks: Prototype credit ledger in allocator service (read-only view + write path) - ENG-823457
Add credit consumption hooks to scheduling path and KV-cache admission - ENG-823458
Implement soft-eviction threshold that triggers credit replenishment probes rather than immediate hard evict
Create chaos tests and synthetic tenant scenarios to validate fairshare under 1x, 5x, and 10x noisy workloads
Add Console dashboard tiles for 'credit balance' and 'eviction backoff events' and attach to SLO alerts
Run a single-pool canary with guardrail: 10% traffic shift and 30m observation window before broader rollout
decisions: Use token-style credits (continuous decrement per GPU-second-equivalent) instead of discrete job slots to better correlate with model cost
Apply a conservative credit decay window of 5 minutes to avoid oscillation during brief spikes
Prefer soft-eviction (reduce burst allowance + requeue) over immediate hard eviction when credit deficit observed
Telemetry-first rollout: ship metrics and dashboards before enabling enforcement

postmortem_summary: Root cause: single tenant workload caused sustained KV cache churn and prefix cache misses leading to eviction storms in colocated dedicated pools. Interim mitigations (manual tenant fencing and reservation bump) reduced immediate pain but are operationally heavy. The fairshare crediting + soft-eviction mechanism reduces coupling between tenant burstiness and global eviction behavior and provides observable signals for gradual enforcement.
rollback_plan: Feature gate off fairshare enforcement via remote config
Drain canary pool and re-enable previous reservation-based rules if abnormal regressions observed
Revert allocator binary to previous stable build and clear credit ledger state after revert
monitoring_goals: Eviction-rate (per-pool and per-tenant) trend shows steady decline within 30 minutes of enforcement
Credit-deficit alert fires when >3 tenants in a pool have deficit >30s
P95/P99 latency regression monitoring with automatic rollback threshold at >10% regression
